post_copy:
In DNR's Houston decision, "conveyance" means about 6,800 acres to AIDEA at no cost, with no specific project approved.

The parcel is down from 19,500 acres and its north line clears the Haessler-Norris trails.
Commenters warned about wells. DNR's reply is that no specific project is approved.
Development stays 100 feet back from three anadromous waters.
Commenters warned about the grid. DNR's reply is that no transmission facilities are authorized.
The state can again take back land not developed for AIDEA's plan.

The conveyance redraws the edges and leaves the water and the power for later.

The new line staked on the real terrain, what the comments moved, the four survey pieces, the restored take-back and what waits for later.

Should wells and the grid get a public answer before the patent issues, or only once a specific project files?

#MatSu #AlaskaDNR #AIDEA

slides.headline: About a third of the July map, at no cost.
slides.body: Commissioner John Crowther signed it November 10th. About 6,800 acres two miles north of Houston go to AIDEA at no cost, so no appraisal is required. The other 12,700 acres stay with DNR.

slides.headline: 2,306 comments moved the north line.
slides.body: DNR redrew the parcel to avoid any overlap with the Haessler-Norris trail system. It says AIDEA intends to keep allowing public access until a patent is issued.
labels: TRAIL SYSTEM, NORTH OF THE NEW LINE

slides.headline: Salmon water gets 100 feet.
slides.body: The decision lists three anadromous waters within or bordering the parcel. Development must stay 100 feet back from each. The south edge sits about half a mile from the Little Susitna River.

slides.headline: Inside the line, nothing is drawn yet.
slides.body: The decision approves no specific project.

slides.headline: Four pieces, on plats from 1915, 1917 and 1963.
labels: DNR ROUNDS THE TOTAL TO ABOUT 6,800 ACRES

slides.headline: July waived the take-back. November keeps it.
slides.body: Land not developed for the purpose in AIDEA's plan reverts to the state. Separately, AIDEA must survey and finish pre-patent work within 10 years, or the decision is void.
labels: A KNOT THAT CAN BE PULLED FREE

slides.headline: 2,306 comments. The wells and the grid wait.
slides.body: Commenters warned of drawn-down wells and a strained grid. DNR answered that the conveyance approves no specific project. Reconsideration requests are due within 20 days, with a $200 fee.

slides.headline: If not in this decision, where do the well and grid questions get answered?

aftercare: Social delivery is automatic this edition under the daily social delivery update, so the Gmail draft is a delivery copy. Don't post it again by hand.
Paste the first comment (the sources block) under the live LinkedIn post within 60 seconds. The automation uploads media only and never comments, so this step is yours.
Reply to every comment in the first 90 minutes, the golden hour. Answer wells, grid and reconsideration questions from the signed decision.
After 48 hours, note saves, comments and reposts for the ledger.
editor_notes_for_email: UPDATE of No.97 and No.88. DNR's signed Final Finding and Decision on ADL 234762 (November 10th) conveys about 6,800 acres near Houston to AIDEA at no cost, down from 19,500 in July. The parcel now avoids the Haessler-Norris trails, keeps a 100 foot setback from three anadromous waters and restores the state's reversionary interest. It approves no specific project and no roads, utilities or transmission. Reconsideration requests are due within 20 calendar days with a $200 fee.
